name: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycle
description: The UK's e-bike: a pedal cycle with any number of wheels and an electric motor of no more than 250 W maximum continuous rated power that can't propel it past 15.5 mph (25 km/h). It isn't a motor vehicle, so it needs no licence, registration, tax or insurance, and anyone 14 or older may ride it wherever pedal cycles go. Northern Ireland has prescribed the same class under its own regulations since May 2020.

restrictions.rule: Pedals that can propel it, on two or more wheels; there's no weight limit
restrictions.citation: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1168, regs. 3-4, as amended by SI 2015/24, reg. 2

restrictions.rule: No motor other than an electric one with a maximum continuous rated power of no more than 250 W, measured as Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 does or by an equivalent EEA standard
restrictions.citation: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1168, regs. 4(c)(i), 5, as amended by SI 2015/24, reg. 2

restrictions.rule: The motor can't propel it once it's travelling faster than 15.5 mph (25 km/h)
restrictions.citation: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1168, reg. 4(c)(ii), as amended by SI 2015/24, reg. 2

restrictions.rule: An 'off road' mode that lets the motor propel it past 15.5 mph takes it out of this class, and it's then a motor vehicle

A throttle may propel it without pedalling up to 15.5 mph, but a 'twist and go' placed on the market or entering service from 1 January 2016 must first be type approved, or get a Motorcycle Single Vehicle Approval as a 250 W low-powered moped; walk assist up to 3.7 mph (6 km/h) needs no approval

Ridden on a road only if it carries either a plate securely fixed in a conspicuous, accessible position showing the manufacturer, the battery's nominal voltage and the motor's continuous rated output, or visible, durable markings of the manufacturer, the fastest the motor can propel it in mph or km/h, and the motor's maximum continuous rated power in watts or kilowatts
restrictions.citation: Pedal Cycles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1176, reg. 4(a), as amended by SI 2015/474, reg. 2(3)

restrictions.rule: Ridden on a road only with a battery that can't leak dangerously, and a power control biased to off that lets the motor run only while it's operated
restrictions.citation: Pedal Cycles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1176, reg. 4(c)-(d), as amended by SI 2015/474, reg. 2(3)

restrictions.rule: Brakes meeting clause 4.6.8 of BS EN ISO 4210-2:2014 or an equivalent standard, or the type-approval braking requirements if it's type approved, kept in efficient working order; it may not be sold without them
restrictions.citation: Pedal Cycles (Construction and Use) Regulations 1983, SI 1983/1176, regs. 4A, 5(b), 12, as amended by SI 2015/474, reg. 2(4)-(6)

restrictions.rule: Between sunset and sunrise, the lights and reflectors of any pedal cycle: a white front lamp, a red rear lamp, a red rear reflector, and amber pedal reflectors on one made from 1 October 1985
The rider must be 14 or older, and it's an offence to let someone known or suspected to be younger ride one on a road
Not a motor vehicle, so it needs no driving licence, registration, vehicle tax or insurance
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 189(1)(c); Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984, s. 140(1)(c); Vehicle Excise and Registration Act 1994, Sch. 2, para. 2A

restrictions.rule: May be ridden on cycle paths and anywhere else pedal cycles are allowed, but not on pavements
restrictions.citation: Road Traffic Act 1988, s. 21(3)(aa); Highway Act 1835, s. 72; Roads (Scotland) Act 1984, ss. 129(5), 151(1)

restrictions.rule: In Northern Ireland, the same class (pedals, two or more wheels, 250 W, 15.5 mph) has been prescribed since 13 May 2020, with the same marking, battery, power-control and brake requirements and the lighting requirements for cycles
restrictions.citation: Electrically Assisted Pedal Cycles (Construction and Use) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2020, SR 2020/31, regs. 3-7; Road Traffic (Northern Ireland) Order 1995, art. 6(1)(c)

restrictions.rule: In Northern Ireland, the rider must also be 14 or older, and needs no registration, licence, insurance or motorcycle helmet; a twist-and-go needs type approval there too
